threads.thread_goal: Align on vision, target segments, and MVP scope for the platform.

messages.text: Team, we're kicking off the eco-tourism platform launch and need to lock in our strategy and MVP scope within the next 21 days. I've reviewed the initial thinking and want to make sure we're aligned on who we're targeting and what we're building. Please review A1 (Eco-Tourism Platform Strategy and MVP Scope) and share your thoughts on target segments and priority regions. We need to confirm D1 and D2 before we move forward with detailed product work.

Thanks for the kickoff. I've looked at A1 and the initial segment analysis. I think we should focus on three primary segments for MVP: affluent eco-conscious travelers (35-55 age), adventure-seeking millennials, and corporate team-building groups. These segments have strong demand signals based on recent market research and align well with our conservation positioning. For regions, I'd recommend starting with Southeast Asia (Thailand, Vietnam) and Central America (Costa Rica, Guatemala) - both have established eco-tourism infrastructure and strong partner networks. This keeps us focused and reduces complexity for the 90-day delivery window. T1 should capture this formally.

I agree with the segment focus. From a product perspective, those three segments make sense for our initial bundles. Southeast Asia and Central America are solid choices - I have existing relationships with several operators in both regions who align with our sustainability criteria. One thing to flag: we'll need to ensure our partner selection process (A3) is tight from day one, especially around environmental compliance. I'm working on T2 (curating the initial bundles) and T6 (partner criteria), and I want to make sure the segments we choose here inform which experiences we prioritize. Should we also consider any geographic constraints around seasonality or regulatory requirements?

Good point on seasonality. I'd add that we need to validate demand for these segments before we lock the bundles. The market research is helpful, but I'd recommend we run quick customer interviews with at least 15-20 prospects in each segment to confirm willingness to pay and feature preferences. This directly supports T1 and reduces risk on D1. We can do this in parallel with T2 and T3 (customer journey design). Once we have that validation, we'll be much more confident in our MVP scope.

I think the segments make sense. I'm looking at the financial implications - if we focus on those three segments, we should model pricing and volume assumptions accordingly. I'll need to work with whoever owns T5 (financial model) to ensure our revenue projections align with realistic conversion rates for each segment. Also, I want to make sure we're tracking the budget envelope early. What's the approved marketing spend for launch?

Marketing budget is capped at the pre-approved envelope - I'll share the exact number in the financial thread (TH3). For now, assume it's tight and we'll need to be strategic about channels. That's part of T7 (go-to-market plan). But first, let's lock the segments. I'm hearing alignment on the three segments and two regions. Should we confirm D1 now, or do we want to wait for the customer validation that 185576 mentioned?

I think we should move forward with D1 now - the segments and regions are well-reasoned and we can validate demand in parallel. The customer interviews 185576 suggested are smart risk mitigation. Let's confirm: primary segments are affluent eco-conscious (35-55), adventure millennials, and corporate groups; priority regions are Southeast Asia and Central America. Does everyone agree?
Agreed. This gives me clear direction for T2 and T6. I'll start curating bundles that appeal to these segments and finalize partner criteria aligned with the regions.

Confirmed. Now let's move to D2 - the MVP feature set. I've drafted initial user stories based on A4 (Customer Journey and Experience Blueprint) and T4 (MVP feature definition). The core features for MVP are: search and filter by experience type and region, booking and payment, customer profile and trip history, basic review and rating system, and post-trip feedback collection. I've prioritized these using MoSCoW - these are all 'Must Have' for launch. Everything else (advanced personalization, loyalty program, multi-language support beyond English/Spanish) goes to post-launch. Does this align with everyone's thinking?

I'd push back slightly on the review and rating system for MVP. I understand the value, but it adds complexity to the backend and moderation overhead. Can we defer that to week 2 post-launch? The core booking, payment, and profile features are essential. Everything else can wait. This keeps us lean and focused on the 90-day delivery window.

Fair point. I'll move reviews to post-launch. So MVP is: search/filter, booking, payment, profile, and post-trip feedback (which is lightweight). That's tighter and more achievable. I'll update T4 with the revised feature list and acceptance criteria. Should we lock D2 on this scope?

Yes, let's confirm D2: MVP features are search/filter, booking, payment, customer profile, and post-trip feedback. No reviews in MVP. 99087, please finalize T4 with user stories and acceptance criteria by EOD tomorrow. 185576, can you validate the customer journey (A4) maps to these features? We need to ensure the experience is seamless end-to-end.

Will do. I'll map the journey to the feature set and flag any gaps. I'll also incorporate the customer validation interviews I mentioned earlier - those insights will help refine the journey and ensure we're designing for real needs.

Got it. With D1 and D2 locked, I can now finalize the financial model assumptions. I'll need to model revenue based on the three segments, two regions, and the MVP feature set. This will feed into T5 and help us confirm the budget envelope in TH3.

Perfect. So to recap TH1: we've confirmed D1 (segments and regions) and D2 (MVP features). Next steps are T1 (finalize segment documentation), T3 (validate and refine customer journey), T4 (complete user stories), and T5 (financial model). I'll prepare a summary message with owners and timelines.

**TH1 Summary - Decisions Made:**

D1: Confirmed primary customer segments (affluent eco-conscious 35-55, adventure millennials, corporate groups) and priority regions (Southeast Asia, Central America).

D2: Approved MVP feature set (search/filter, booking, payment, profile, post-trip feedback). Reviews deferred to post-launch.

**Next Steps:**
- T1 (segment documentation): 99087, EOD tomorrow
- T3 (customer journey validation): 185576, EOD tomorrow
- T4 (user stories and acceptance criteria): 99087, EOD tomorrow
- T5 (financial model): 22473, by end of week
- Customer validation interviews: 185576, start today

All artifacts (A1, A4) will be updated to reflect these decisions.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate eco-tourism bundles, partner criteria, and service standards.

messages.text: I've drafted the initial eco-tourism bundles for MVP and want to share them for feedback. I've curated 10 bundles across Southeast Asia and Central America, each mapped to our three target segments. I've also prepared A3 (Partner Selection and Sustainability Criteria) and started work on A6 (Service Standards for On-Site Experiences). The bundles are in the spreadsheet linked below, and I'd like feedback on bundle mix, pricing ranges, and sustainability alignment before we finalize for D3.

Great work. I've reviewed the bundles and they look solid. A few observations: the pricing ranges seem reasonable relative to competitive offers, and I like how you've mapped each bundle to sustainability criteria. One question: how are you handling seasonality? Some of these experiences (e.g., the rainforest treks in Costa Rica) have strong seasonal demand. Should we adjust availability or pricing by season in the MVP, or keep it simple for launch?

Good catch. For MVP, I'm recommending we keep it simple - fixed pricing and availability by bundle, with a note that some experiences are seasonal. We can add dynamic pricing and seasonal adjustments in a post-launch iteration. This keeps the platform logic lean and lets us focus on the core booking flow. I've documented this assumption in T2.

I agree on keeping it simple for MVP. From a customer experience perspective, I'd suggest we clearly communicate seasonal availability in the bundle description and search filters. That way, customers aren't surprised when they book. I'll incorporate this into the journey map (A4) and feature requirements (T4).

Perfect. Now, on the partner criteria (A3) - I've drafted a checklist covering environmental standards, safety certifications, service quality, and community benefit. I want to make sure we're not being too restrictive (which would limit our bundle options) but also not too loose (which could damage our brand). I've included criteria like: certified sustainable tourism operators, local community employment targets, and environmental impact assessments. Should we add anything else, or does this feel right?

The criteria look solid. I'd add one more: compliance with local tourism regulations in each region. We need to ensure our partners have all required permits and licenses. This is a risk mitigation point - if a partner loses their license, we need to know immediately. I'd also suggest we build a compliance review step into the partner onboarding process (T6). This should be documented and tracked.

Agreed. I'll add regulatory compliance to A3 and build it into the onboarding checklist in T6. I'm also working on A6 (Service Standards) which will define expectations for partners across pre-trip, on-trip, and post-trip phases. This will help ensure consistent quality across all bundles. I'm planning to share a draft of A6 by tomorrow for feedback.

Good. For A6, I'd suggest we include specific service standards that map to the customer journey touchpoints. For example: pre-trip communication (response time, clarity), on-trip experience (guide quality, safety protocols), and post-trip follow-up (feedback collection, issue resolution). This ensures the service standards directly support the customer experience we're designing.

Perfect. I'll structure A6 around those journey phases. I'm also planning to pilot the service standards with 3 partners in each region (6 total) before we finalize. This is part of T10 - I want to get real feedback on whether the standards are realistic and achievable. Should we lock the bundle selection (D3) before or after the pilot feedback?

I'd say we can lock D3 (bundle selection) now based on the current draft, but make it conditional on partner feedback from T10. If the pilot reveals that certain bundles are hard to deliver to our service standards, we can adjust. This keeps us moving forward without waiting for the pilot to complete. We can finalize the bundle list once we have partner feedback, but we don't need to delay the decision.

Agreed. Let's confirm D3: we're moving forward with the 10 bundles as drafted, pending partner feedback from the pilot. 52126, can you finalize the bundle list and partner criteria (A3) by EOD tomorrow? And 99087, I want you to review A3 and confirm it aligns with our risk mitigation strategy. We also need to lock D4 (partner criteria approval) before we start outreach.

Will do. I'll review A3 against our risk register and confirm it covers regulatory compliance, environmental standards, and community benefit. I'll also flag any gaps or dependencies. 52126, once you share the final A3, I'll turn around feedback by EOD tomorrow.

**TH2 Summary - Decisions Made:**

D3: Approved 10 eco-tourism bundles for MVP (across Southeast Asia and Central America, mapped to three target segments). Bundles are conditional on partner feedback from pilot (T10).

D4: Approved Partner Selection and Sustainability Criteria (A3) including environmental standards, safety, service quality, community benefit, and regulatory compliance. Criteria will be integrated into partner onboarding process (T6).

**Next Steps:**
- A3 (Partner Criteria): finalize by 52126, EOD tomorrow
- A6 (Service Standards): draft by 52126, EOD tomorrow
- T6 (Partner Onboarding): 52126, by end of week
- T10 (Pilot Partner Feedback): 52126, start outreach today
- A3 Review: 99087, EOD tomorrow

All artifacts will be updated and linked in the project index.

threads.thread_goal: Lock pricing approach, financial assumptions, and budget envelope.

messages.text: I've prepared a preliminary financial model (A2) with revenue and cost projections for the first 12 months. I've modeled three scenarios: base case (conservative conversion rates), optimistic (higher adoption), and conservative (slower ramp). The model assumes the three customer segments and two regions we locked in TH1, and incorporates the 10 bundles from TH2. I need feedback on pricing strategy, volume assumptions, and cost structure before we confirm the budget envelope. Please review A2 and share thoughts.

I've reviewed A2. The model looks reasonable overall, but I have a few questions on the assumptions. First, what's the pricing strategy - are we positioning as premium, mid-market, or value? This affects both revenue and customer acquisition cost. Second, the conversion rate assumptions (2% base, 4% optimistic) seem reasonable, but I'd like to validate them against the customer interviews 185576 is running. Third, on costs - I see platform development, marketing, and partner commissions. Are we accounting for customer support and operational overhead?

Good questions. On pricing: I'd recommend we position as premium but accessible - we're not the cheapest option, but we're offering curated, sustainable experiences with strong community benefit. This justifies a 15-20% price premium over generic eco-tourism offers. On conversion rates: yes, let's validate against customer interviews. I'd also suggest we A/B test landing pages with different value propositions to get real conversion data. On costs: we should include customer support (at least 1 FTE for MVP), payment processing fees, and a contingency buffer.

I agree on the premium positioning. From a customer perspective, the willingness to pay for sustainable, community-focused experiences is strong - especially in the affluent eco-conscious segment. I'm incorporating this into the customer interviews and will have initial data by end of week. I'd also recommend we test messaging around community impact and conservation - that's a key differentiator for our target segments.

Okay, so premium positioning with 15-20% price premium. That makes sense. Let me update A2 with: (1) revised pricing assumptions, (2) customer support and operational costs, (3) payment processing fees, (4) contingency buffer. I'll also add a sensitivity analysis to show how changes in conversion rate or average order value impact margin. Should I also model different launch scenarios - e.g., phased rollout vs. full launch?

Yes, include a phased rollout scenario. I want to see the financial impact of launching in Southeast Asia first, then Central America 4 weeks later. This reduces risk and lets us learn from the first market before scaling. Also, what's the total budget envelope we need for MVP build and launch marketing? I need to confirm this with the board.

I'll model the phased rollout. Based on the current assumptions, the total budget envelope for MVP build (platform development, design, QA) and launch marketing is approximately 450K-500K depending on the scenario. This includes platform development (250K), marketing (120K), partner onboarding and support (80K), and contingency (50K). I'll have the detailed breakdown in the updated A2 by EOD tomorrow.

That budget feels reasonable for a 90-day MVP launch. The platform development cost is in line with typical SaaS builds, and the marketing budget is tight but achievable given our pre-approved cap. I'd suggest we allocate the marketing budget strategically: 40% to direct customer acquisition (landing page, paid search), 30% to partner enablement (training, collateral), and 30% to PR and content (thought leadership, conservation stories). This aligns with our premium positioning and community focus.

I like that allocation. The partner enablement and PR/content spend will help us build credibility and differentiation. I'd also suggest we reserve some budget for customer acquisition testing - landing page A/B tests, messaging tests, channel tests. This will give us real data to optimize the go-to-market plan (T7) and inform post-launch scaling.

Good point. I'll build in a 10% testing budget within the marketing allocation. So the breakdown is: 36% direct acquisition, 27% partner enablement, 27% PR/content, 10% testing. I'll finalize A2 with this allocation and the phased rollout scenario by EOD tomorrow. Once I have that, we can lock D5 (pricing strategy and financial assumptions) and D6 (budget envelope).

Perfect. 22473, once you finalize A2, I'll review it and confirm the budget envelope with the board. In the meantime, let's assume the 450K-500K range is approved. This will let us move forward with T5 (financial model finalization) and T9 (executive alignment). I want to lock D5 and D6 by EOD tomorrow so we can move to the next phase.
Will do. I'll have A2 finalized by EOD tomorrow with all scenarios, assumptions, and budget breakdown. I'll also prepare a one-page executive summary for the board review.

**TH3 Summary - Decisions Made:**

D5: Approved pricing strategy (premium positioning with 15-20% price premium over generic eco-tourism). Financial assumptions include: 2% base conversion rate, 4% optimistic; customer support and operational costs included; payment processing fees and contingency buffer included.

D6: Confirmed budget envelope of 450K-500K for MVP build and launch marketing. Allocation: 36% direct acquisition, 27% partner enablement, 27% PR/content, 10% testing. Phased rollout scenario (Southeast Asia first, Central America 4 weeks later) approved.

**Next Steps:**
- A2 (Financial Model): finalize by 22473, EOD tomorrow
- T5 (Financial Model): 22473, EOD tomorrow
- T9 (Executive Alignment): 472565, by end of week
- Customer validation interviews: 185576, ongoing

Board review scheduled for end of week.

threads.thread_goal: Prioritise backlog, define KPIs, and prepare handover to delivery teams.

messages.text: I've updated the MVP backlog (A5) with prioritized user stories and dependencies, and I've drafted the KPI framework (A8) for launch tracking. The backlog is organized by MoSCoW priority: Must Have (core booking, payment, profile), Should Have (post-trip feedback, basic search filters), Could Have (advanced filters, multi-language), and Won't Have (reviews, loyalty program). For KPIs, I've defined metrics across four categories: acquisition (traffic, conversion), engagement (bookings, average order value), satisfaction (NPS, support tickets), and impact (community benefit, conservation metrics). I'd like feedback on both before we finalize for D7 and D8.

Good structure. I've reviewed A5 and the backlog looks solid. One thing I'd flag: the dependencies between user stories. For example, the payment feature depends on the booking feature, which depends on search. I want to make sure the delivery team understands the critical path and can sequence the work correctly. Can you add a dependency diagram or critical path analysis to A5?

Good catch. I'll add a dependency matrix to A5 showing which features block which. The critical path is: search -> booking -> payment -> profile. Everything else (post-trip feedback, filters) can be developed in parallel. I'll also add effort estimates (story points) so the delivery team can plan sprints.

From a product perspective, I want to make sure the backlog reflects the bundle and partner requirements. For example, the search feature needs to support filtering by region, experience type, and sustainability criteria. The booking feature needs to capture partner-specific requirements (e.g., group size limits, age restrictions). Can you add these product requirements to the user stories in A5?

Absolutely. I'll add product requirements to each user story. For search: region, experience type, sustainability criteria, price range, availability. For booking: partner-specific constraints, group size, age restrictions, special requests. I'll also add acceptance criteria that map to the partner service standards (A6) so the delivery team knows what 'done' looks like.

Perfect. Now on the KPI framework (A8) - I've reviewed it and it's comprehensive. I'd add one more category: operational KPIs (partner onboarding time, support response time, platform uptime). These will help us track the health of the platform and partner ecosystem post-launch. Also, for the impact KPIs, I'd suggest we define them more specifically - e.g., 'percentage of revenue shared with local communities' or 'number of local jobs created per experience'.

Great suggestions. I'll add operational KPIs and refine the impact metrics. For impact, I'll define: percentage of revenue to communities, local jobs created, conservation acres protected, and community satisfaction score. I'll also add data sources and owners for each KPI so we know who's responsible for tracking. This will be in the updated A8.

I want to make sure the KPIs align with the financial model (A2). For example, the acquisition KPIs (traffic, conversion) should map to the revenue assumptions in A2. The satisfaction KPIs (NPS, support tickets) should help us understand customer lifetime value and churn. Can you cross-reference A8 with A2 so we can track financial performance against KPIs?

Good point. I'll add a mapping table in A8 that shows how each KPI connects to the financial model assumptions. For example: conversion rate KPI maps to revenue assumptions, average order value KPI maps to pricing assumptions, customer acquisition cost KPI maps to marketing budget. This will help us track whether we're on track financially.

Excellent. So we're locking D7 (MVP backlog priorities) and D8 (KPI framework). 99087, I need you to finalize A5 and A8 by EOD tomorrow with all the updates we discussed. Once that's done, we need to prepare the handover package for the delivery team. T11 says we need to organize all artifacts and schedule a walkthrough. Can you coordinate that?

Will do. I'll finalize A5 and A8 by EOD tomorrow. For T11, I'll create a project index with all artifacts linked and organized by theme (strategy, product, financial, KPIs). I'll also schedule a handover walkthrough with the delivery leads for day after tomorrow. This will give them time to review the artifacts and ask questions.

I'll support the handover walkthrough. I can walk through the customer journey (A4) and explain how the backlog user stories map to the journey stages. This will help the delivery team understand the 'why' behind each feature.
And I'll walk through the partner and product requirements. I want to make sure the delivery team understands the constraints and dependencies with our partners.

**TH4 Summary - Decisions Made:**

D7: Froze MVP backlog priorities using MoSCoW framework. Must Have: search, booking, payment, profile. Should Have: post-trip feedback, filters. Could Have: advanced filters, multi-language. Won't Have: reviews, loyalty. Backlog includes dependency matrix, effort estimates, and product requirements mapped to partner constraints.

D8: Approved KPI framework across four categories: acquisition (traffic, conversion), engagement (bookings, AOV), satisfaction (NPS, support), operational (uptime, response time), and impact (community revenue share, jobs created, conservation acres). KPIs mapped to financial model assumptions.

**Next Steps:**
- A5 (Backlog): finalize by 99087, EOD tomorrow
- A8 (KPI Framework): finalize by 99087, EOD tomorrow
- T11 (Handover Package): 99087, by end of week
- Handover Walkthrough: 99087, 185576, 52126, day after tomorrow
- T12 (Risk Register): 472565, by end of week

All artifacts linked in project index.

threads.thread_goal: Align on go-to-market narrative, channels, and launch milestones.

messages.text: I've drafted the go-to-market and channel plan (A7) for the MVP launch. The plan outlines our launch narrative (curated, sustainable, community-focused eco-tourism), primary acquisition channels (direct, agencies, platforms), and a high-level campaign calendar aligned with the pre-approved marketing budget. I've also mapped the plan to our target segments and regions. I'd like feedback on the narrative, channel prioritization, and launch timeline before we finalize D9 and D10.

I've reviewed A7 and the narrative is strong. I like the emphasis on community benefit and conservation - that's a key differentiator for our target segments. One question: how are we positioning against existing eco-tourism platforms? What's our unique value proposition? I want to make sure the messaging is clear and compelling.

Good question. Our unique value proposition is: curated experiences (not a marketplace of all operators), transparent community benefit (customers see where their money goes), and verified sustainability (all partners meet our criteria). This is different from generic platforms like Airbnb Experiences or Viator, which are broader and less focused on impact. I'll sharpen the messaging in A7 to emphasize these differentiators.

I like that positioning. From a partner perspective, I want to make sure we're also communicating the value to operators - e.g., access to a curated customer base, marketing support, fair commission structure. This will help us attract quality partners and differentiate from other platforms. Can you add a partner value proposition to A7?

Absolutely. I'll add a partner value proposition section to A7: access to quality customers, marketing co-investment, fair commission (I'm assuming 20-25% based on A2?), and operational support. This will be part of the partner enablement messaging.

Yes, 20-25% commission is in the financial model. I'd also suggest we offer tiered commissions - e.g., 20% for new partners, 18% for partners who hit volume targets. This incentivizes growth and rewards loyalty. I'll update A2 with this structure.

Good idea. I'll incorporate the tiered commission structure into the partner value proposition in A7. Now, on channels: I'm recommending we prioritize direct (landing page, paid search, email) and agencies (travel agencies, corporate travel) for MVP launch. Platforms (Airbnb, Viator) can come later once we have more reviews and social proof. Does this make sense?

I agree. Direct and agencies are lower friction for launch and give us more control over the customer experience. Platforms can be a post-launch expansion. I'd also suggest we invest in content marketing - blog posts, case studies, conservation stories - to build credibility and SEO. This supports the direct channel and differentiates us from generic platforms.

Perfect. I'll add content marketing to the channel plan. Now, on timeline: I'm proposing a phased launch aligned with the financial model. Week 1-2: soft launch in Southeast Asia (Thailand, Vietnam) with limited inventory and partner outreach. Week 3-4: full launch in Southeast Asia with marketing push. Week 5-6: launch in Central America. This gives us time to learn and iterate. Does this timeline work?

That timeline works. It aligns with the phased rollout scenario in the financial model and reduces risk. I want to confirm: soft launch is internal/partner-only, full launch is public? And we need to define what 'go/no-go' criteria are for each phase. If we don't hit certain KPI targets in Southeast Asia, do we proceed to Central America or pause?

Good point. Yes, soft launch is partner-only with limited public access. For go/no-go criteria, I'd suggest: conversion rate >= 1.5%, customer satisfaction (NPS) >= 40, and zero critical bugs. If we hit these in Southeast Asia, we proceed to Central America. If not, we pause and iterate. I'll add this to A7 and also to T12 (risk register).

I'd also add a go/no-go criterion around partner satisfaction. If partners are struggling with the onboarding or service standards, we should pause and fix before scaling. This ensures we're not just optimizing for customer metrics but also partner health.

Absolutely. I'll add partner satisfaction (NPS >= 35) as a go/no-go criterion. So the full set is: customer conversion >= 1.5%, customer NPS >= 40, partner NPS >= 35, zero critical bugs. I'll finalize A7 with this timeline and criteria by EOD tomorrow.

Perfect. Let's lock D9 (launch date window and milestones) and D10 (primary acquisition channels). D9: phased launch starting week 1 (soft launch Southeast Asia), week 3 (full launch Southeast Asia), week 5 (Central America). Go/no-go criteria: customer conversion >= 1.5%, customer NPS >= 40, partner NPS >= 35, zero critical bugs. D10: primary channels are direct (landing page, paid search, email) and agencies (travel agencies, corporate travel). Content marketing as supporting channel. Does everyone agree?

Agreed. I'll finalize A7 with the timeline, go/no-go criteria, and channel strategy by EOD tomorrow. I'll also prepare a one-page launch checklist for the team so everyone knows what needs to be done before each phase.

**TH5 Summary - Decisions Made:**

D9: Confirmed phased launch timeline. Week 1-2: soft launch Southeast Asia (partner-only, limited inventory). Week 3-4: full launch Southeast Asia (public, marketing push). Week 5-6: launch Central America. Go/no-go criteria: customer conversion >= 1.5%, customer NPS >= 40, partner NPS >= 35, zero critical bugs.

D10: Approved primary acquisition channels: direct (landing page, paid search, email) and agencies (travel agencies, corporate travel). Content marketing as supporting channel. Partner value proposition includes tiered commission structure (20% base, 18% for volume partners).

**Next Steps:**
- A7 (Go-to-Market Plan): finalize by 99087, EOD tomorrow
- T7 (Channel Strategy): 99087, EOD tomorrow
- T9 (Executive Alignment): 472565, by end of week
- Launch checklist: 99087, by end of week

All artifacts linked in project index. Pre-launch go/no-go review scheduled for week 1.
